  OPEN SESSION ITEMS

  1. CONDITIONAL USE PERMIT NO. 24-74 TO ALLOW AN UPGRADE OF AN ABC LICENSE TYPE 20 (OFF-SALE OF
  BEER AND WINE) TO A LICENSE TYPE 21 (OFF-SALE, GENERAL; OFF-SALE OF BEER, WINE, AND DISTILLED
  SPIRITS), INCLUDING A NEW ANCILLARY LICENSE TYPE 86 (INSTRUCTIONAL TASTING LICENSE) IN
  CONJUNCTION WITH AN EXISTING LARGE FORMAT RETAIL DEPARTMENT/GROCERY STORE (“TARGET”)
  LOCATED AT 5700 FIRESTONE BOULEVARD.

  Planning Manager John Signo introduced Senior Planner Rodrigo Pelayo who
  gave a presentation on the proposed conditional use permit (CUP). Mr. Pelayo
  showed the location of the site, gave an overview of the proposed use, and
  discussed the proposed operation.

  Chair Ozaeta opened the public hearing and asked the applicant to come
  forward.

  Beth Aboulafia, applicant on behalf of Target Corporation, spoke in support of
  the proposed use and provided additional information. She indicated that
  Target has been selling beer and wine at this location since 2005. There are

Planning Commission Minutes 12.3.24
  Page 1 of 3  4
   around eight Target stores that have already obtained approval for instructional
  tasting and more to come. An event to launch instructional tasting at Target
  stores throughout the regional will occur sometime in 2025.

  Recording Secretary Kimberly Hernandez indicated there was one email
  received from Mario Dominguez. She read the email into the record. Mr.
  Dominguez asked about other locations in which instructional tasting would
  occur and requested that Target consider donating towards South Gate Park.

  Commissioner Daisy Prieto disclosed that her adult daughter is a temporary
  employee at Target.

  Commissioner Lizette Ruiz asked about security and the involvement of the
  Police Department.

  Ms. Aboulafia indicated there is video surveillance and other crime prevention
  measures in place. Target is willing to work with the Police Department to deter
  and prevent crime.

  Chair Jimmy Ozaeta asked about the licenses pending at other cities and where
  they are located.

  Ms. Aboulafia indicated most stores are in Los Angeles County. Most are newer
  stores and include locations in Compton, Gardena, Long Beach, Norwalk,
  Pomona, San Pedro, and others. Signage will be provided to indicate patrons
  must be at least 21 years old. She indicated the person stationed at the tasting
  area would have to enforce the age limit to prevent minors from taking part,
  however, since Target has not yet operated an instructional tasting event,
  protocols will still need to be developed.

  Chair Ozaeta asked if this would be a liability for Target.

  Ms. Aboulafia explained that Target would be liable if there are violations. There
  currently are no protocols, but Target is committed to following the
  requirements established by the Department of Alcoholic Beverage Control
  (ABC).

  Commissioner Ruiz asked about oversight mechanisms such as using decoys to
  test protocols. She asked if the CUP can be revoked.

  With no other comments, Chair Ozaeta closed the public hearing.

  Resolution 2024-08
  ACTION:  Approved 5-0. Motion by Commissioner Perez.
  Seconded by Commissioner Prieto.

  CONDITIONAL USE PERMIT (CUP) TO ALLOW THE SALES OF ALCOHOL (ABC LICENSE TYPE 41 - BEER AND

  WITHIN A SOCCER FACILITY AT 9599 PINEHURST AVE (THE “SOFIVE SOCCER COMPLEX”), AND FINDING THAT
  THE PROJECT IS CATEGORICALLY EXEMPT FROM THE CEQA UNDER SECTION 15301, (CLASS 1) “EXISTING

  Presentation by Rodrigo Pelayo, Senior Planner

  Mike Ayaz, representative/attorney for Sofive Soccer Complex (“Sofive”), spoke
  and thanked staff. He indicated they have worked with the community and have
  support from members of the city of Covina in which they operate another
  facility. They have reviewed the conditions and will be able to comply with them
  as well as with the lease and requirements from the Department of Alcoholic

  He indicated there are others in the audience in support of the project. Sofive
  has invested in the community and provides jobs.

  Louis Gerbier, applicant for Sofive Soccer Complex, explained the operations at
  the facility and indicated they have reached out to the community. He explained
  that anyone who wants alcohol needs to provide identification and can only
  consume alcohol in the designated space.

  Steve Costley, Director of Parks and Recreation for the City of South Gate,
  indicated Sofive has been good neighbors and his staff is in the area to monitor
  issues. He expressed his support for the project.

  Caroline Maravilla, 9311 Hildreth Avenue, indicated there are a lot of issues with
  alcohol and the police do not show up. She provided a petition and expressed
  issues with safety. She stated alcohol should not be permitted at this location.

  Olivia Quijano, 9604 Pinehurst Avenue, stated she lives across the street from
  Sofive and objects to alcohol sales at Sofive.

  Edgar Pelayo, resident and Parks and Recreation Commissioner, discussed safety
  concerns and stated police do not respond. He stated Sofive is responsible for
  the batting cages which are not maintained well. He does not support the
  project.

  Edgar Aleman, 10024 Annetta Avenue, indicated the project could bring benefits
  due to economic growth, revenue, job creation, tax revenue, and enhance the
  park’s experience. He prefers the project over people bringing their own alcohol
  to the park. He stated his support for the project.

  Ana Elizarraras, Director of South Gate Chamber of Commerce, expressed her
  support for the project.

  Al Rios, resident on Orange Street, stated he has nothing personal about Sofive,
  but is concerned about the expansion under new ownership. He stated Council
  was not aware and Council voted the project down a couple of years ago. He
  stated concerns about the batting cages which Sofive is responsible for and
  there is already drinking occurring at the park. He stated he has concerns with
  public safety and the risks involved.

  Leo Quijano II, son of former Parks and Recreation Commissioner, indicated
  concerns with the school on Pinehurst across the street. He stated the principal
  is not opposed because Sofive allows school kids onto the facility for free. He is
  concerned with alcohol at the facility with kids present.

  Juan Perez, resident, indicated he was at Tuesday’s meeting about Target and
  does not see much difference. He stated he approves of the project.

  [Name not provided by Spanish speaker; Senior Planner Pelayo provided

  Alicia, general manager for Sofive, stated school kids do use their fields during

  Olga Vega, stated she is a resident of thirty years next to South Gate Park. She

  Vice Chair Laborin asked if the petition was included at the last meeting.

  •  Mario Dominguez Jr. wrote in support of project in separate messages.

  Assistant City Attorney Hardwick answered “yes.”

  Commissioner Ruiz asked about security and cameras.

  Mr. Ayaz indicated their facility in the city of Covina serves alcohol and security
  measures work. City can review the use in six months.

   Vice Chair Laborin disclosed she visited the Covina site and contacted
  representatives from the City.

  Mr. Ayaz indicated extra staff can be brought in during special events. The
  parking lot will be monitored. The goal is to keep patrons safe. There has not
  been a change in ownership.

  Vice Chair Laborin asked about service at Covina.

  Mr. Ayaz indicated staff is trained on intoxication.

  Commissioner Perez thanked everyone for showing up. She pointed out
  Condition No. 32 regarding revocation if the use is in violation. She indicated it is

  Vice Chair Laborin indicated the Police Department works with the Department
  of Alcohol and Beverage Control (ABC).

  Commissioner Prieto thanked the applicants, staff, and the community. She
  indicated security will be provided inside the building. She asked about “happy
  hour” and the party room.

  Mr. Ayaz indicated the party room is meant for events such as birthday parties.
  Alcohol will not be served to kids. It can be used as a meeting room.

  Chair Ozaeta spoke about public participation. He indicated residents have
  spoken to him about concerns with alcohol. He asked about the responsibility
  and maintenance of the batting cages.

  Commissioner Perez reiterated that the batting cages were not functional.

  Vice Chair Laborin stated she heard they were fixed.

  Assistant City Attorney Hardwick urged the Commission to focus on the
  proposal for alcohol sales.

  City Manager Houston indicated the lease was recently renewed and
  maintenance on the batting cages is a part.

  Chair Ozaeta asked about the designated versus shared parking lot.

  Senior Planner Pelayo indicated they need to maintain the parking lot, but some
  are shared some are not exclusive – maintenance does fall on the City.

  Chair Ozaeta asked about the conditions.

  Senior Planner Pelayo indicated staff had discussions with the applicant as well
  as the Police Department and Parks staff.

  Planning Manager Signo indicated staff strives to work with the applicant on the
  conditions so there is consensus prior to bringing the item to the Commission.

   Chair Ozaeta asked about the last sale at 10:00 p.m. The new condition allows
  sales to 10:30 p.m. even though the facility closes at 11:00 p.m. He asked about
  security guards.

  Assistant City Attorney Hardwick explained the applicant had referenced two
  security staff in the application. Staff drafted the conditions based on this
  statement.

  City Manager Houston indicated staff typically does not dictate business
  operations and staffing but wanted to ensure safety in the neighborhood.
  Condition No. 32 allows staff to decide if there are any issues what can be done.

  Assistant City Attorney Hardwick pointed out Condition No. 29.

  Chair Ozaeta indicated the application stated there would be two security
  guards. He stated he visited the facility and staff and the facility are amazing. He
  sees the asset the facility brings to the community. It is there for recreational
  purposes and not to serve alcohol. He stated his concern with alcohol sales at
  Sofive.

SUBJECT: 2024 YEAR IN REVIEW AND REPORT ON PLANNING DIVISION
ACTIVITIES

PURPOSE: To provide the Planning Commission an overview of the accomplishments,
challenges, and goals of the Planning Division and Planning Commission during 2024 and provide
an update on planning projects and division procedures.

BACKGROUND:
The Planning Division is responsible for processing development applications in the City based
on the zoning regulations found in Title 11 of the South Gate Municipal Code. The City has
established several zones, each with its own development standards. These zones are grouped into
three broad categories: urban mixed-use zones; commercial industrial zones; and residential
neighborhood zones. Many types of projects can be approved by staff at the administrative level.
However, certain projects and land uses require discretionary review by the Planning Commission.
These include conditional use permits, variances, and site plan reviews. Actions by staff
(Community Development Director) are appealable to the Planning Commission, and actions by
the Planning Commission are appealable to the City Council.

Some of the challenges faced by the Planning Division include the retention of staff. There has
been high turnover throughout 2024, especially at the beginning of the year when planners were
leaving about every month. To fill the void, contract planners were hired to process applications
but their contracts would eventually end and replacements would have to pick up where the project
was left off. Currently, the Planning Division is fully staffed with four full-time employees which
includes a planning manager, senior planner, associate planner, and assistant planner.

ANALYSIS:

Planning Counter
The Community Development Department uses QLess as an electronic sign in for customers at
the front counter. The system was setup after the start of the pandemic to limit contact between
customers and staff. Customers are able to sign in electronically, wait in their cars or in the lobby,
and be summoned to the counter when they are next in line. QLess makes it easy to track the
number of customers coming to the front counter.

Some common questions asked by the public include:

  •  What is my property zoned?

  33
   •  How do I build an addition or an accessory dwelling unit (ADU)?
  •  How do I submit a development application?
  •  How long does the development process take?
  •  When do I receive a permit?
  •  What land uses are permitted on my property?
  •  How do I get a sign permit for my business?
  •  What developments are occurring in South Gate?

In 2024, there were a total of 2,599 customers that came to the Planning counter. This averages to
about 216.6 customers per month or 12-13 customers per day. Roughly 92.4% of the customers
proceed with their appointment with others who are removed (either on their own or by another
division), leave, or do not show up.

Planning Projects
Staff had undertaken several improvements in 2024 to make it easier to track projects and
communicate with residents. Among those included starting a PL (Planning) case numbering
system around July 2024 to better track incoming projects and updating databases to keep track of
those projects. Staff recorded 763 residential projects (e.g., additions, accessory structures, etc.),
157 commercial projects, 13 entitlements (e.g., conditional use permits, variances, etc.), and 18
miscellaneous projects (e.g., zoning verifications). Of the 763 residential projects, there were 233
accessory dwelling units (ADUs) and 4 Senate Bill 9 (SB9) projects.

Simple applications such as roof repairs, roof-mounted solar panels, and interior remodels are done
over-the-counter the same day. For questionable or complex applications, the planner may take a
week to review the application. For projects that require administrative review, applications are

  34
 received electronically and the planner has 30 days under the Permit Streamlining Act to notify
the applicant if the application is complete. Plans are also routed to other departments such as
Building, Public Works, Police, and Fire for review. If incomplete, the planner lets the applicant
know in writing what is missing and also includes lists discrepancies where the project does not
comply with development standards.

For discretionary projects such as conditional use permits and variances that require Planning
Commission approval, the planner still reviews the application for completeness and conformance
within the first 30 days. Once complete, the planner prepares the application for a public hearing
with the Planning Commission and notices are published in the newspaper and mailed to residents
within 1,000 feet of the subject property. The timeframe to schedule a hearing with the Planning
Commission is about 6-8 months provided the project is exempt from the California Environmental
Quality Act (CEQA). If the project is not exempt and preparation of a mitigated negative
declaration (MND) or environmental impact report (EIR) is required, the process will take much
longer often over a year.
